title: How Conventional PKC Reads Both Branches

scenes.tts: The first film left I P three traveling and D A G in the membrane. How can conventional protein kinase C use both branches? The branches reach the same cell but keep different locations. Return to the same cell and follow one kinase. Follow its movement and timing.
scenes.caption: The first film left IP3 traveling and DAG in the membrane. How can conventional protein kinase C use both branches? The branches reach the same cell but keep different locations. Return to the same cell and follow one kinase. Follow its movement and timing.
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 schematic cell cross-section and exact COLOR MAP: PIP2 GOLD; IP3 BLUE; DAG ORANGE; calcium GREEN; PLC WHITE; conventional PKC TEAL; Gq route PURPLE; receptor-tyrosine-kinase route MAGENTA. The BLUE IP3 path still reaches the ER, GREEN calcium dots drift upward, and ORANGE DAG sways in the plasma membrane. A folded TEAL PKC cartoon enters the cytosol. It is one connected chain of labelled blocks, not a molecular structure. On the question, green and orange arrows point toward it. Keep 'schematic' at bottom right.
scenes.narration: The first film left IP3 traveling and DAG in the membrane. How can conventional protein kinase C use both branches? The branches reach the same cell but keep different locations. Return to the same cell and follow one kinase. Follow its movement and timing.

scenes.visual: Title 'How Conventional PKC Reads Both Branches' fades in over the moving cell world for two seconds. Green calcium drifts, orange DAG sways, and the folded teal kinase slowly rotates.

scenes.tts: At rest, conventional P K C is folded shut. Its pseudosubstrate occupies the kinase active site, blocking real substrates. All four parts are connected in one protein chain. A C two domain can respond to calcium. A C one domain can recognize D A G.
scenes.caption: At rest, conventional PKC is folded shut. Its pseudosubstrate occupies the kinase active site, blocking real substrates. All four parts are connected in one protein chain. A C2 domain can respond to calcium. A C1 domain can recognize DAG.
scenes.visual: Zoom onto the TEAL PKC cartoon until it fills most of the frame. Four connected blocks read 'pseudosubstrate', 'C1', 'C2', and 'kinase'. The pseudosubstrate block plugs a visible slot labelled 'active site'. A neutral substrate block approaches, bumps the plug, and drifts away. C2 gains a GREEN outline; C1 gains an ORANGE outline.
scenes.narration: At rest, conventional PKC is folded shut. Its pseudosubstrate occupies the kinase active site, blocking real substrates. All four parts are connected in one protein chain. A C2 domain can respond to calcium. A C1 domain can recognize DAG.

scenes.tts: I P three opened the endoplasmic reticulum channel, raising cytosolic calcium. Calcium binds C two and changes its membrane affinity. C two then engages anionic lipids, bringing conventional P K C toward the plasma membrane. The kinase is now close enough to sample the local membrane.
scenes.caption: IP3 opened the endoplasmic reticulum channel, raising cytosolic calcium. Calcium binds C2 and changes its membrane affinity. C2 then engages anionic lipids, bringing conventional PKC toward the plasma membrane. The kinase is now close enough to sample the local membrane.
scenes.visual: Pull back enough to show ER and plasma membrane. BLUE IP3 opens the ER gate again. GREEN calcium dots stream out; three gather around the GREEN-edged C2 block without implying exact stoichiometry. The entire folded PKC glides upward. C2 touches a broad membrane patch labelled 'anionic lipids', while the pseudosubstrate remains in the active-site slot.
scenes.narration: IP3 opened the endoplasmic reticulum channel, raising cytosolic calcium. Calcium binds C2 and changes its membrane affinity. C2 then engages anionic lipids, bringing conventional PKC toward the plasma membrane. The kinase is now close enough to sample the local membrane.

scenes.tts: At the membrane, C one can search for D A G. D A G binding strengthens membrane engagement and helps displace the pseudosubstrate. The active site opens, so the kinase can phosphorylate protein substrates.
scenes.caption: At the membrane, C1 can search for DAG. DAG binding strengthens membrane engagement and helps displace the pseudosubstrate. The active site opens, so the kinase can phosphorylate protein substrates.
scenes.visual: The ORANGE-edged C1 block sweeps laterally along the membrane like a small scanner. It meets an ORANGE DAG block and grips it. The PKC chain unfolds enough for the pseudosubstrate plug to slide out of the active-site slot. A neutral substrate block enters the now-open slot and receives a small phosphate badge. Keep C2 touching the anionic-lipid patch.
scenes.narration: At the membrane, C1 can search for DAG. DAG binding strengthens membrane engagement and helps displace the pseudosubstrate. The active site opens, so the kinase can phosphorylate protein substrates.

scenes.tts: Now compare three schematic conditions: calcium without D A G, D A G without raised calcium, and both branches together. Which condition should retain conventional P K C most strongly at this membrane?
scenes.caption: Now compare three schematic conditions: calcium without DAG, DAG without raised calcium, and both branches together. Which condition should retain conventional PKC most strongly at this membrane?
scenes.visual: Divide the carried membrane into three wide panels without changing the world. Labels read 'calcium', 'DAG', and 'calcium + DAG'. Place one identical folded TEAL PKC below each. The inputs appear as GREEN dots, an ORANGE DAG block, or both. A question spans the top: 'Strongest membrane retention?' No panel receives an answer yet.
scenes.narration: Now compare three schematic conditions: calcium without DAG, DAG without raised calcium, and both branches together. Which condition should retain conventional PKC most strongly at this membrane?

scenes.visual: Deliberate predict pause. Hold the three conditions and question. Each PKC bobs gently below its membrane; inputs shimmer. Do not move any kinase to the membrane or reveal strength.

scenes.tts: Each contact alone can be weak under physiological conditions. Together, their binding energies add, so membrane preference can rise sharply. Conventional P K C gives a stronger, longer response where calcium targeting and D A G activation overlap.
scenes.caption: Each contact alone can be weak under physiological conditions. Together, their binding energies add, so membrane preference can rise sharply. Conventional PKC gives a stronger, longer response where calcium targeting and DAG activation overlap.
scenes.visual: In the calcium panel, C2 touches briefly and the PKC drifts back; label 'weaker'. In the DAG panel, C1 samples briefly and releases; label 'weaker'. In the combined panel, C2 and C1 engage together, the kinase stays, unfolds, and phosphorylates a substrate; label 'stronger'. Use no rejected marks, binary lamps, or invented numbers. Slow arrows show graded retention.
scenes.narration: Each contact alone can be weak under physiological conditions. Together, their binding energies add, so membrane preference can rise sharply. Conventional PKC gives a stronger, longer response where calcium targeting and DAG activation overlap.

scenes.tts: This is not a perfectly simultaneous digital switch. Calcium can recruit the kinase rapidly, before D A G engages C one. The response is graded, not all or none. The detector integrates timing as well as place.
scenes.caption: This is not a perfectly simultaneous digital switch. Calcium can recruit the kinase rapidly, before DAG engages C1. The response is graded, not all or none. The detector integrates timing as well as place.
scenes.visual: Merge the panels into one membrane and add a computed-from-script qualitative timeline labelled 'schematic', with no numeric axes. A GREEN calcium band rises first; an ORANGE DAG band rises and overlaps it. The TEAL PKC reaches the membrane with the green rise, then grips orange DAG; its activity glow is brightest and longest across the overlap and dims gradually as the inputs decline. Show no claim about activity after calcium has fallen. Avoid an exact cutoff or an on/off lamp.
scenes.narration: This is not a perfectly simultaneous digital switch. Calcium can recruit the kinase rapidly, before DAG engages C1. The response is graded, not all or none. The detector integrates timing as well as place.

scenes.tts: The rule belongs to conventional P K C. Novel P K C has a C one module suited to D A G-driven recruitment without calcium. Atypical P K C responds to neither messenger and instead uses protein partners.
scenes.caption: The rule belongs to conventional PKC. Novel PKC has a C1 module suited to DAG-driven recruitment without calcium. Atypical PKC responds to neither messenger and instead uses protein partners.
scenes.visual: Three large labelled cartoons slide into a row: 'conventional', 'novel', and 'atypical'. Conventional keeps GREEN C2 and ORANGE C1 outlines. Novel shows an ORANGE C1 outline and a neutral C2-like block. Atypical shows neutral regulatory blocks plus a labelled 'protein partner' block. Animate each toward the membrane only under the input described; keep outcomes graded and schematic.
scenes.narration: The rule belongs to conventional PKC. Novel PKC has a C1 module suited to DAG-driven recruitment without calcium. Atypical PKC responds to neither messenger and instead uses protein partners.

scenes.tts: A phorbol ester can occupy the D A G site and activate P K C directly. Unlike D A G, it is cleared slowly. Prolonged activation can lead to kinase degradation, so signal duration changes the outcome.
scenes.caption: A phorbol ester can occupy the DAG site and activate PKC directly. Unlike DAG, it is cleared slowly. Prolonged activation can lead to kinase degradation, so signal duration changes the outcome.
scenes.visual: Return to conventional PKC at the membrane. Replace the ORANGE DAG block with a striped ORANGE block labelled 'phorbol ester'. A clock face spins while the striped block remains. The active TEAL kinase gradually fades into a few smaller fragments labelled 'degradation'; do not show a tumor or claim a universal cancer direction.
scenes.narration: A phorbol ester can occupy the DAG site and activate PKC directly. Unlike DAG, it is cleared slowly. Prolonged activation can lead to kinase degradation, so signal duration changes the outcome.

scenes.tts: Return once more to the membrane. Calcium changes C two-dependent targeting. D A G changes C one-dependent activation and retention. Keep this rule: conventional P K C integrates calcium targeting with D A G activation at membranes.
scenes.caption: Return once more to the membrane. Calcium changes C2-dependent targeting. DAG changes C1-dependent activation and retention. Keep this rule: conventional PKC integrates calcium targeting with DAG activation at membranes.
scenes.visual: Restore the original cell cross-section and colour legend. GREEN calcium dots carry a TEAL conventional PKC toward the plasma membrane. ORANGE DAG engages C1; the pseudosubstrate leaves and one substrate receives a phosphate badge. Two arrows, 'targeting' in GREEN and 'activation' in ORANGE, merge into one TEAL arrow labelled 'conventional PKC output'.
scenes.narration: Return once more to the membrane. Calcium changes C2-dependent targeting. DAG changes C1-dependent activation and retention. Keep this rule: conventional PKC integrates calcium targeting with DAG activation at membranes.

scenes.visual: Dim the same moving cell world. Show one centred line only, exactly: 'Conventional PKC integrates calcium targeting with DAG activation at membranes.' GREEN calcium drifts and ORANGE DAG sways behind the TEAL kinase.
